title: Hamming SECDED Decoder
constraints: Bit layout (Hamming position → `code` bit): p1→`code[0]`, p2→`code[1]`, d0→`code[2]`, p4→`code[3]`, d1→`code[4]`, d2→`code[5]`, d3→`code[6]`; overall parity p0→`code[7]`.
`data = {d3, d2, d1, d0}`, corrected if there is a single-bit error.
Exactly one of these holds: no error (both flags 0), `single_err = 1` (any one of the 8 bits flipped, including p0), or `double_err = 1` (two bits flipped; `data` is then the uncorrected data bits).
hints: Syndrome bit s1 is the XOR of positions 1, 3, 5, 7; s2 of positions 2, 3, 6, 7; s4 of positions 4, 5, 6, 7. The syndrome `{s4, s2, s1}` is the position of a single error.
The overall parity P = XOR of all 8 bits tells you whether an *odd* number of bits flipped.

P = 1 → single error at position `syndrome` (syndrome 0 means p0 itself flipped). P = 0 with a non-zero syndrome → double error. Flip a data bit only when the syndrome points at positions 3, 5, 6 or 7.
